key_insight: MIRROR exploits mismatches between text, image, and combined views of the same geometry problem to transfer successful reasoning across modalities and make VLM reasoning more consistent.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical training recipe for multimodal systems that need robust, view-invariant reasoning, especially in geometry-style QA and diagram understanding.
method: Build ODA-Data with paired text-dominant, image-dominant, and image+text versions of the same geometry problems.
Run the model on all views, pick the best-performing view as a teacher, and optimize the others toward it with a reverse-KL objective.
Use self-supervised reciprocal reasoning optimization to improve both accuracy and cross-modal consistency.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that ODA-Data includes training/evaluation splits for modality-dependent behaviors and that MIRROR improves over standard RL on geometry reasoning benchmarks.
watch_item: The approach depends on having reliable per-view performance differences and high-quality paired multimodal data, so gains may weaken if the views are poorly aligned or the teacher view is wrong.
paper_title: MIRROR: Learning from the Other View for Multi-Modal Reasoning
